provenance.note: `Operations` takes an `OperationsDeps` — one `fetch` method — so the reference's own class is driven against a recorder, exactly as the pinned `coring.test.ts` drives it. Nothing here derives a key or reads a clock.

declarations.throw_if_failed: private throwIfFailed(op: Operation): asserts op is CompletedOperation { if ('error' in op && op.error !== null) { const details = op.error.details ? ` Details: ${JSON.stringify(op.error.details)}` : ''; throw new Error( `Operation '${op.name}' failed [Code ${op.error.code}]: ${op.error.message}${details}` ); } }
declarations.has_depends: private hasDepends(op: Operation): op is ( | RegistryOperation | CredentialOperation | DelegatorOperation ) & { metadata: NonNullable< ( | RegistryOperation | CredentialOperation | DelegatorOperation )['metadata'] >; } { return op.metadata !== undefined && 'depends' in op.metadata; }

notes.paths: get and delete address the same path and differ only by method; list builds its query with `URLSearchParams` and always appends `?`, even when there is nothing after it
notes.failure: `throwIfFailed` turns a completed-but-failed operation into a thrown string carrying the name, the code, the message, and — when present — the details as JSON
notes.depends: `hasDepends` is a run-time `'depends' in op.metadata`, which the fourteen-way union cannot express statically; the dependency chain it feeds is Roadmap 7.2's

failures.note: `throwIfFailed` is private, so the failure messages are reached through `wait` on an already-completed operation, which returns immediately without polling

pinned_confirmations.note: the three paths the pinned `coring.test.ts` asserts are all produced here by the reference's own methods

list_always_appends_a_question_mark.note: `list()` builds its query with `URLSearchParams` and interpolates `?${params.toString()}` unconditionally, so a list with no filter addresses `/operations?` — a bare question mark with nothing after it. The pinned unit test asserts exactly that string.
list_always_appends_a_question_mark.rust_decision: not reproduced: Roadmap 5.3's path builder emits a query only when there is one, so an unfiltered list addresses `/operations`. An empty query is not a distinguishable resource, the signed path is `/operations` either way — Roadmap 3.10 strips the query before signing — and a KERIA agent parses the two identically.

path_components_are_not_encoded.note: an operation name is interpolated into the path with no encoding, so a name carrying `/` or `?` addresses a different resource entirely — the same defect Roadmap 5.3 recorded across the endpoint families and pinned four executions of
path_components_are_not_encoded.rust_decision: refused by construction: Roadmap 5.3's `ResourcePath` encodes every dynamic component exactly once and offers no way to skip it.

query_values_are_not_encoded_by_the_path.note: the type filter *is* encoded, because `URLSearchParams` does it — one of only two encoded dynamic values in the whole reference, which Roadmap 5.3 counted
query_values_are_not_encoded_by_the_path.rust_decision: reproduced: the path builder encodes it too, so the two agree on this one.

failure_is_a_thrown_string.with_details: Operation 'witness.EMQQpnSkgfUOgWdzQTWfrgiVHKIDAhvAZIPQ6z3EAfz1.0' failed [Code 408]: Timed out waiting for witness receipts Details: {"received":2,"expected":3}
failure_is_a_thrown_string.note: a completed-but-failed operation becomes one interpolated message carrying the name, the code, the message, and the details as JSON; nothing structured survives
failure_is_a_thrown_string.rust_decision: typed: `ClientError::OperationFailed` keeps the name, the code, the message, and the details apart, and the message is bounded because it is remote text.

delete_discards_its_response.note: `delete` awaits the fetch and returns `void`, so a caller learns nothing about what happened beyond the absence of a throw
delete_discards_its_response.rust_decision: reproduced: the Rust method returns `Result<(), ClientError>`, since the status check is what carries the outcome.

get_returns_the_untyped_union.note: `get` returns the fourteen-way `Operation` union, which a caller must narrow by inspecting `metadata` at run time — `hasDepends` is the reference's own example of that
get_returns_the_untyped_union.rust_decision: Roadmap 4.1 already replaced the union with `Operation<M, R>` plus an `UntypedOperation`; `get` returns the untyped form and `get_typed` narrows it, so the narrowing is a decode rather than a property test.
